articles.title: Your AI support agent will invent a price it was never told — here's the 3-section fix
articles.excerpt: A friend runs a 40-seat restaurant. Last month he wired an AI agent into his booking inbox. Within 4 days it had quoted a customer "$45 per person, all-in, drinks included" for a set menu that costs $…
articles.body: A friend runs a 40-seat restaurant. Last month he wired an AI agent into his booking inbox. Within 4 days it had quoted a customer "$45 per person, all-in, drinks included" for a set menu that costs $68. It also promised a same-day refund policy his restaurant has never had. The agent didn't hallucinate because it was dumb. It hallucinated because nothing in its context told it where "the truth" ended and "what a helpful assistant would say" began . Ask an LLM for a price it has never seen and it will produce the most plausible-sounding number. Plausible is the problem: your customer can't tell the difference until they arrive. I've now deployed this pattern in service businesses, restaurants, and online stores. The fix is not a better model or a longer prompt.
articles.author: chenwengui23

articles.title: Aurelia
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass Aurelia is a digital-detox game for Android that is boring on purpose. It gives you quests that can't be finishe…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built Aurelia is a digital-detox game for Android that is boring on purpose. The whole interface is black-and-white terminal text: ASCII progress bars, a pixel butterfly, oversized level numbers. The color lives outside, which is the point. It gives you quests that can't be finished on the couch. Spot a bird. Photograph a mushroom. Find the strangest texture within a hundred steps. You take a photo as evidence, and a neural network running entirely on the phone checks what is actually in the frame. Verified finds pay XP; at 440 XP your companion reaches IMAGO, its final form. Completed quests fill a photo journal, the only part of the app allowed to show color.

articles.title: Build Infrastructure Is a Trust Anchor: Threat Modelling Exposed CI/CD and Artifact Repositories
articles.excerpt: Build Infrastructure Is a Trust Anchor: Threat Modelling Exposed CI/CD and Artifact Repositories A build server holds the credentials that sign, package and publish your software. An artifact reposito…
articles.body: Build Infrastructure Is a Trust Anchor: Threat Modelling Exposed CI/CD and Artifact Repositories A build server holds the credentials that sign, package and publish your software. An artifact repository holds the packages your production systems install. Neither is a peripheral system, and both are frequently reachable from networks they were never meant to face. Treating them as ordinary internal services is the modelling error. They are trust anchors: compromising one lets an attacker produce software that your own pipelines will accept. The reachable population Measurements taken on 20 September 2026 show how much of this class is internet-observable.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . Nature Quest (pocket edition) is taking Gemma 4 E2B outside into the outdoor environment with no internet connection, fully Offline. What I Built Pocket Nature Quest is a fully offline Android field companion that turns one outdoor photo into a short Look · Listen · Move quest. The idea is deliberately a little paradoxical: use AI on a phone to encourage someone to stop looking at their phone . Help user achieve wellness by observing their natural environment. The screen is only the starting point. A user takes a photo, optionally adds GPS context, chooses a time and energy level, and receives three simple actions to complete outside.

articles.title: Khoj: Step Outside With a Question, Come Back With a Story
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass Khoj is an open-source, offline-first AI exploration companion that turns a walk around your city into a curiosi…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass Khoj (खोज) — Don't Follow the Map. Follow Your Curiosity. What I Built Khoj is an open-source, offline-first AI exploration companion that turns a walk around your city into a curiosity-driven adventure. It's easy to spend hours exploring a city through a screen without actually experiencing the world around us. I wanted to build something that encourages the opposite: put your phone away, step outside, pay attention to your surroundings, and discover something new. Starting with Mumbai, Khoj helps people: 🧭 Choose an exploration duration and an area of interest. 🌿 Get a curiosity-driven mission inspired by a curated city knowledge pack.

articles.title: The card application wanted a history I did not have yet
articles.excerpt: The first card I applied for asked for an SSN or an ITIN, and I was proud to have the second one. I typed the nine digits that start with 9 and waited. The answer was polite and quick: not enough cred…
articles.body: The first card I applied for asked for an SSN or an ITIN, and I was proud to have the second one. I typed the nine digits that start with 9 and waited. The answer was polite and quick: not enough credit history. I had a taxpayer number. I did not have a file. Those are two different things, and I had treated them as one. The ITIN lets the IRS match a return to a person without a Social Security number. It is not work authorization, and it is not a credit score. A score needs a file, and a file needs accounts that report. The order I skipped ITIN Club writes the order down plainly, and I did not invent it: get the ITIN, open a US bank account that will take it, start a credit file, let a score exist, and only then look at the cards with the travel points.

articles.title: How to Evaluate the ROI of AI Automation Before Investing
articles.excerpt: AI automation can create meaningful business value, but only when the use case is chosen carefully and measured honestly. Many organisations overestimate savings because they count theoretical hours i…
articles.body: AI automation can create meaningful business value, but only when the use case is chosen carefully and measured honestly. Many organisations overestimate savings because they count theoretical hours instead of real capacity, or they underestimate costs because they ignore integration, governance and change management. A good ROI model prevents both mistakes. Business owners and operations leaders do not need a machine learning degree to evaluate AI automation. They need a practical way to compare current process cost, expected benefit, delivery complexity, risk and time to value. 4 inputs - Baseline cost, benefit estimate, implementation cost and operating risk. 3 benefits - Cost reduction, throughput improvement and quality or revenue lift.

articles.title: NASA dumped over 800GB of Artemis II data online
articles.excerpt: A crew annotated image showing where the Artemis II team observed impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. | Image: NASA If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission,…
articles.body: A crew annotated image showing where the Artemis II team observed impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. | Image: NASA If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission , you're wrong. This week NASA posted over 800GB worth of science data, images, and videos on the Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science site. The archive includes over 11,000 photos and videos, over 8.5 hours of audio, and crew-annotated images, such as the one marking where they saw impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. Together, they offer an unprecedented view inside a historic space mission. One of the more exciting reveals was footage of the Artemis II team telling the ground team back in Houston about its observation of impact flashes.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Lunar Farside Explanation: Tidally locked in synchronous rotation , the Moon always presents its familiar nearside to denizens of planet Earth . articles.body: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested an executive at a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity. The New York Times reported today that the FBI has arrested a Canadian man in Pennsylvania on suspicion of assisting ShinyHunters. The Times story did not identify the man, nor did a statement on Twitter/X about the arrest from FBI Director Kash Patel .
